title: IL SB1507: VEH CD-SAFETY ZONES

obligations: A municipality that produces a recorded image of a motor vehicle's violation must make the recorded images accessible to the alleged violator by providing a website address accessible through the Internet. (Sec. 11-208.8(b))

For each violation recorded, the municipality having jurisdiction shall issue a written notice of the violation to the registered owner of the vehicle as the alleged violator, delivered by mail within 30 days after the Secretary of State notifies the municipality of the identity of the owner, but in no event later than 90 days after the violation. (Sec. 11-208.8(e))

The notice must include the name and address of the registered owner, registration number, violation charged, date, time, and location, a copy of the recorded image or images, the amount of the civil penalty and due date, a statement that recorded images are evidence, a warning that failure to pay or contest is an admission of liability, a statement of options to pay or challenge, and a website address to view the recorded images. (Sec. 11-208.8(f))

A roadway equipped with an automated speed enforcement system shall be posted with a sign conforming to the national Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices that is visible to approaching traffic stating that vehicle speeds are being photo-enforced and indicating the speed limit. The municipality shall install additional signage as it determines necessary to give reasonable notice. (Sec. 11-208.8(l))

A roadway where a new automated speed enforcement system is installed shall be posted with signs providing 30 days notice of the use of a new system prior to the issuance of any citations. (Sec. 11-208.8(m))

The compensation paid for an automated speed enforcement system must be based on the value of the equipment or the services provided and may not be based on the number of traffic citations issued or the revenue generated by the system. (Sec. 11-208.8(n))

A municipality using an automated speed enforcement system must provide notice to drivers by publishing the locations of all safety zones where system equipment is installed on the website of the municipality. (Sec. 11-208.8(q))

A municipality operating an automated speed enforcement system shall conduct a statistical analysis to assess the safety impact of the system following installation and every 2 years thereafter. If operating before the effective date of the 103rd General Assembly amendatory Act, the analysis must be completed by no later than one year after that effective date and every 2 years thereafter. The analysis must be based on the best available crash, traffic, and other data, cover a period before and after installation sufficient for statistically valid comparison, be consistent with professional judgment and acceptable industry practice, and be made available to the public and published on the municipality's website. (Sec. 11-208.8(r))

The net proceeds that a municipality receives from civil penalties, after deducting all non-personnel and personnel costs associated with operation and maintenance of the system, shall be expended or obligated for public safety initiatives to ensure safe passage around schools and provide police protection and surveillance around schools and parks, initiatives to improve pedestrian and traffic safety, construction and maintenance of infrastructure including roads and bridges, and after school programs. (Sec. 11-208.8(d))

If a county or municipality selects a new vendor for its automated speed enforcement system and must apply for a permit, approval, or other authorization from the Department for reinstallation of one or more malfunctioning components, and the new vendor operates an automated speed enforcement system for any other county or municipality in the State, the Department shall approve or deny the application within 90 days after receipt. (Sec. 11-208.8(t))

The Department may revoke any permit, approval, or other authorization granted to a county or municipality for placement, installation, or operation of an automated speed enforcement system if any official or employee who serves that county or municipality is charged with bribery, official misconduct, or a similar crime related to the placement, installation, or operation of the system. The Department shall adopt rules for the revocation process, notice, and appeal, and any entity with a revoked permit may not reapply for 1 year. (Sec. 11-208.8(u))

The University of Illinois Chicago Urban Transportation Center shall conduct a study including a comprehensive review of City of Chicago website multi-year crash data on North and South DuSable Lake Shore Drive, available research on potential effectiveness of cameras powered by artificial intelligence in improving compliance and reducing crashes and road fatalities on that roadway, an analysis of driving behavior to detect risky driving patterns and address crash corridors, an assessment of effectiveness of psychological deterrence in reducing habitual speeding, and an assessment of how fatalities can be reduced using AI cameras and other technical options. (Sec. 11-208.8(v))
prohibitions: A penalty may not be imposed under this Section if the recorded speed of a vehicle is 5 miles per hour or less over the legal speed limit. (Sec. 11-208.8(c))

A penalty may not be imposed if the driver of the motor vehicle received a Uniform Traffic Citation from a police officer for a speeding violation occurring within one-eighth of a mile and 15 minutes of the violation recorded by the system. (Sec. 11-208.8(c))

The automated speed enforcement system shall be operational and violations shall be recorded only at the following times: if the safety zone is based upon school district property, only on school days and no earlier than 6 a.m. and no later than 8:30 p.m. Monday through Thursday, or 9 p.m. on Friday; if based upon park district property, no earlier than one hour prior to opening and no later than one hour after closing. (Sec. 11-208.8(a-5))
Compensation for an automated speed enforcement system may not be based on the number of traffic citations issued or the revenue generated by the system. (Sec. 11-208.8(n))

No member of the General Assembly and no officer or employee of a municipality or county shall knowingly accept employment or receive compensation or fees for services from a vendor that provides automated speed enforcement system equipment or services to municipalities or counties. No former member of the General Assembly shall, within 2 years after termination of service, knowingly accept such employment or compensation. No former officer or employee of a municipality or county shall, within 2 years after termination of employment, knowingly accept such employment or compensation. (Sec. 11-208.8(n-1))

No person who is the lessor of a motor vehicle pursuant to a written lease agreement shall be liable for an automated speed or traffic law enforcement system violation involving such motor vehicle during the period of the lease, provided that upon request received within 120 days after the violation, the lessor provides within 60 days the name and address of the lessee. (Sec. 11-208.8(p))
The term safety zone does not include any portion of the roadway known as Lake Shore Drive or any controlled access highway with 8 or more lanes of traffic. (Sec. 11-208.8(a))
reading.what_it_does: This Illinois law regulates automated speed enforcement systems in safety zones near schools and parks. It applies only to municipalities with a population of 1,000,000 or more.
key_definitions: Automated speed enforcement system: a photographic device, radar device, laser device, or other electrical or mechanical device or devices installed or utilized in a safety zone and designed to record the speed of a vehicle and obtain a clear photograph or other recorded image of the vehicle and the vehicle's registration plate or digital registration plate while the driver is violating Article VI of Chapter 11 of this Code or a similar provision of a local ordinance. An automated speed enforcement system is a system, located in a safety zone which is under the jurisdiction of a municipality, that produces a recorded image of a motor vehicle's violation of a provision of this Code or a local ordinance and is designed to obtain a clear recorded image of the vehicle and the vehicle's license plate. The recorded image must also display the time, date, and location of the violation. (Sec. 11-208.8(a))
Owner: the person or entity to whom the vehicle is registered. (Sec. 11-208.8(a))

Recorded image: images recorded by an automated speed enforcement system on: (1) 2 or more photographs; (2) 2 or more microphotographs; (3) 2 or more electronic images; or (4) a video recording showing the motor vehicle and, on at least one image or portion of the recording, clearly identifying the registration plate or digital registration plate number of the motor vehicle. (Sec. 11-208.8(a))

Safety zone: an area that is within one-eighth of a mile from the nearest property line of any public or private elementary or secondary school, or from the nearest property line of any facility, area, or land owned by a school district that is used for educational purposes approved by the Illinois State Board of Education, not including school district headquarters or administrative buildings. However, if any portion of a roadway is within either one-eighth mile radius, the safety zone also shall include the roadway extended to the furthest portion of the next furthest intersection. What it does

This Illinois law regulates automated speed enforcement systems in safety zones near schools and parks. It defines safety zones, sets operational time limits, requires notice to vehicle owners, imposes civil penalties for speeding violations recorded by the systems, and mandates signage, data confidentiality, statistical analysis, and restrictions on vendor compensation and employment. It applies only to municipalities with a population of 1,000,000 or more.

Who it applies to

  • Municipalities with a population of 1,000,000 or more inhabitants that operate automated speed enforcement systems in safety zones
  • Registered owners of motor vehicles recorded speeding in safety zones
  • Vendors providing automated speed enforcement system equipment or services to municipalities or counties
  • Lessors of motor vehicles under written lease agreements
  • The Department referenced in the statute
  • The University of Illinois Chicago Urban Transportation Center

Effective date

not stated in the text

Key definitions

  • Automated speed enforcement system: a photographic device, radar device, laser device, or other electrical or mechanical device or devices installed or utilized in a safety zone and designed to record the speed of a vehicle and obtain a clear photograph or other recorded image of the vehicle and the vehicle's registration plate or digital registration plate while the driver is violating Article VI of Chapter 11 of this Code or a similar provision of a local ordinance. An automated speed enforcement system is a system, located in a safety zone which is under the jurisdiction of a municipality, that produces a recorded image of a motor vehicle's violation of a provision of this Code or a local ordinance and is designed to obtain a clear recorded image of the vehicle and the vehicle's license plate. The recorded image must also display the time, date, and location of the violation. (Sec. 11-208.8(a))
  • Owner: the person or entity to whom the vehicle is registered. (Sec. 11-208.8(a))
  • Recorded image: images recorded by an automated speed enforcement system on: (1) 2 or more photographs; (2) 2 or more microphotographs; (3) 2 or more electronic images; or (4) a video recording showing the motor vehicle and, on at least one image or portion of the recording, clearly identifying the registration plate or digital registration plate number of the motor vehicle. (Sec. 11-208.8(a))
  • Safety zone: an area that is within one-eighth of a mile from the nearest property line of any public or private elementary or secondary school, or from the nearest property line of any facility, area, or land owned by a school district that is used for educational purposes approved by the Illinois State Board of Education, not including school district headquarters or administrative buildings. A safety zone also includes an area that is within one-eighth of a mile from the nearest property line of any facility, area, or land owned by a park district used for recreational purposes. However, if any portion of a roadway is within either one-eighth mile radius, the safety zone also shall include the roadway extended to the furthest portion of the next furthest intersection. The term safety zone does not include any portion of the roadway known as Lake Shore Drive or any controlled access highway with 8 or more lanes of traffic. (Sec. 11-208.8(a))

Obligations

  • A municipality that produces a recorded image of a motor vehicle's violation must make the recorded images accessible to the alleged violator by providing a website address accessible through the Internet. (Sec. 11-208.8(b))
  • For each violation recorded, the municipality having jurisdiction shall issue a written notice of the violation to the registered owner of the vehicle as the alleged violator, delivered by mail within 30 days after the Secretary of State notifies the municipality of the identity of the owner, but in no event later than 90 days after the violation. (Sec. 11-208.8(e))
  • The notice must include the name and address of the registered owner, registration number, violation charged, date, time, and location, a copy of the recorded image or images, the amount of the civil penalty and due date, a statement that recorded images are evidence, a warning that failure to pay or contest is an admission of liability, a statement of options to pay or challenge, and a website address to view the recorded images. (Sec. 11-208.8(f))
  • A roadway equipped with an automated speed enforcement system shall be posted with a sign conforming to the national Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices that is visible to approaching traffic stating that vehicle speeds are being photo-enforced and indicating the speed limit. The municipality shall install additional signage as it determines necessary to give reasonable notice. (Sec. 11-208.8(l))
  • A roadway where a new automated speed enforcement system is installed shall be posted with signs providing 30 days notice of the use of a new system prior to the issuance of any citations. (Sec. 11-208.8(m))
  • The compensation paid for an automated speed enforcement system must be based on the value of the equipment or the services provided and may not be based on the number of traffic citations issued or the revenue generated by the system. (Sec. 11-208.8(n))
  • A municipality using an automated speed enforcement system must provide notice to drivers by publishing the locations of all safety zones where system equipment is installed on the website of the municipality. (Sec. 11-208.8(q))
  • A municipality operating an automated speed enforcement system shall conduct a statistical analysis to assess the safety impact of the system following installation and every 2 years thereafter. If operating before the effective date of the 103rd General Assembly amendatory Act, the analysis must be completed by no later than one year after that effective date and every 2 years thereafter. The analysis must be based on the best available crash, traffic, and other data, cover a period before and after installation sufficient for statistically valid comparison, be consistent with professional judgment and acceptable industry practice, and be made available to the public and published on the municipality's website. (Sec. 11-208.8(r))
  • The net proceeds that a municipality receives from civil penalties, after deducting all non-personnel and personnel costs associated with operation and maintenance of the system, shall be expended or obligated for public safety initiatives to ensure safe passage around schools and provide police protection and surveillance around schools and parks, initiatives to improve pedestrian and traffic safety, construction and maintenance of infrastructure including roads and bridges, and after school programs.   • If a county or municipality selects a new vendor for its automated speed enforcement system and must apply for a permit, approval, or other authorization from the Department for reinstallation of one or more malfunctioning components, and the new vendor operates an automated speed enforcement system for any other county or municipality in the State, the Department shall approve or deny the application within 90 days after receipt. (Sec. 11-208.8(t))
  • The Department may revoke any permit, approval, or other authorization granted to a county or municipality for placement, installation, or operation of an automated speed enforcement system if any official or employee who serves that county or municipality is charged with bribery, official misconduct, or a similar crime related to the placement, installation, or operation of the system. The Department shall adopt rules for the revocation process, notice, and appeal, and any entity with a revoked permit may not reapply for 1 year. (Sec. 11-208.8(u))

(Sec. 11-208.8(v))

Prohibitions

  • A penalty may not be imposed under this Section if the recorded speed of a vehicle is 5 miles per hour or less over the legal speed limit. (Sec. 11-208.8(c))
  • A penalty may not be imposed if the driver of the motor vehicle received a Uniform Traffic Citation from a police officer for a speeding violation occurring within one-eighth of a mile and 15 minutes of the violation recorded by the system. (Sec. 11-208.8(c))
  • The automated speed enforcement system shall be operational and violations shall be recorded only at the following times: if the safety zone is based upon school district property, only on school days and no earlier than 6 a.m. and no later than 8:30 p.m. Monday through Thursday, or 9 p.m. on Friday; if based upon park district property, no earlier than one hour prior to opening and no later than one hour after closing. (Sec. 11-208.8(a-5))
  • Compensation for an automated speed enforcement system may not be based on the number of traffic citations issued or the revenue generated by the system. (Sec. 11-208.8(n))
  • No member of the General Assembly and no officer or employee of a municipality or county shall knowingly accept employment or receive compensation or fees for services from a vendor that provides automated speed enforcement system equipment or services to municipalities or counties. No former member of the General Assembly shall, within 2 years after termination of service, knowingly accept such employment or compensation. No former officer or employee of a municipality or county shall, within 2 years after termination of employment, knowingly accept such employment or compensation. (Sec. 11-208.8(n-1))
  • No person who is the lessor of a motor vehicle pursuant to a written lease agreement shall be liable for an automated speed or traffic law enforcement system violation involving such motor vehicle during the period of the lease, provided that upon request received within 120 days after the violation, the lessor provides within 60 days the name and address of the lessee. (Sec. 11-208.8(p))
  • The term safety zone does not include any portion of the roadway known as Lake Shore Drive or any controlled access highway with 8 or more lanes of traffic. (Sec. 11-208.8(a))

Penalties and enforcement

The municipality having jurisdiction issues the written notice of violation and imposes civil penalties. Penalties are: if recorded speed is 6 to 10 mph over the limit, a civil penalty not exceeding $50, plus an additional penalty of not more than $50 for failure to pay timely; if more than 10 mph over, a civil penalty not exceeding $100, plus an additional penalty of not more than $100 for late payment. A violation for which a civil penalty is imposed is not a violation of a traffic regulation governing movement of vehicles and may not be recorded on the driving record of the owner. A law enforcement officer is not required to be present or witness the violation. The court or hearing officer may consider defenses including that the vehicle or plates were stolen or hijacked before the violation and not under owner's control, that the driver received a Uniform Traffic Citation within one-eighth mile and 15 minutes, and any other evidence or issues provided by municipal ordinance. The Department may revoke permits for systems if an official or employee is charged with bribery or official misconduct, with rules for revocation, notice, and appeal, and a 1-year reapplication ban. No private right of action is stated in the text. (Sec. 11-208.8(c), (e), (h), (i), (j), (k), (u))

How it affects AI deployment

  • An organisation deploying automated speed enforcement systems that use AI or other technology in covered municipalities must ensure the system meets the statutory definition and is located only in a safety zone as defined, excluding Lake Shore Drive and controlled access highways with 8 or more lanes. (Sec. 11-208.8(a))
  • The system may record violations only during the specified time windows based on school or park district property, so AI-enabled enforcement outside those hours is prohibited. (Sec. 11-208.8(a-5))
  • The organisation must provide a website address for alleged violators to access recorded images, include all required notice content, and deliver notices within the statutory deadlines. (Sec. 11-208.8(b), (e), (f))
  • Recorded images produced by the system, including any AI-processed images, are confidential and may be used only for adjudication, statistical, or governmental purposes, limiting data sharing or commercial use. (Sec. 11-208.8(i))
  • The organisation must post signage conforming to the national Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices and provide 30 days notice before a new system issues citations. (Sec. 11-208.8(l), (m))
  • Vendor compensation cannot be based on citations or revenue, so AI system vendors cannot be paid per citation. Employment restrictions prohibit current and former government officials from working for vendors within specified periods. (Sec. 11-208.8(n), (n-1))
  • The organisation must publish safety zone locations on its website and conduct and publish a statistical safety impact analysis every 2 years, which may require evaluating AI system effectiveness. (Sec. 11-208.8(q), (r))
  • If the organisation is a municipality with population under 1,000,000, this Section does not apply, so AI speed enforcement in safety zones is not authorized under this law. (Sec. 11-208.8(s))
  • The University of Illinois Chicago Urban Transportation Center must study AI-powered cameras on Lake Shore Drive, but Lake Shore Drive is excluded from safety zones, so automated speed enforcement, including AI, cannot be deployed there under this Section. (Sec. 11-208.8(a), (v))

  • Lessors under written lease agreements are not liable for violations during the lease period if they provide lessee information within required timeframes. (Sec. 11-208.8(p))
  • Safety zones do not include Lake Shore Drive or any controlled access highway with 8 or more lanes of traffic. (Sec. 11-208.8(a))
  • No penalty may be imposed if recorded speed is 5 mph or less over the legal speed limit. (Sec. 11-208.8(c))
  • No penalty may be imposed if the driver received a Uniform Traffic Citation from a police officer for a speeding violation occurring within one-eighth of a mile and 15 minutes of the recorded violation. (Sec. 11-208.8(c))

Compliance steps

  • Determine whether the municipality has a population of 1,000,000 or more, as this Section applies only to such municipalities. (Sec. 11-208.8(s))

  • Maintain confidentiality of recorded images, allowing access only to alleged violator and governmental/law enforcement agencies for permitted purposes. (Sec. 11-208.8(i))
  • Structure vendor compensation based on value of equipment or services, not on citations or revenue, and ensure no prohibited employment relationships with vendors. (Sec. 11-208.8(n), (n-1))
  • Publish locations of all safety zones with system equipment on the municipality website. (Sec. 11-208.8(q))
  • Conduct and publish a statistical safety impact analysis after installation and every 2 years, using best available data and professional standards. (Sec. 11-208.8(r))
  • If selecting a new vendor requiring Department approval for reinstallation, submit application and expect decision within 90 days. (Sec. 11-208.8(t))
  • Comply with Department rules on permit revocation, including avoiding charges of bribery or official misconduct by officials or employees. (Sec. 11-208.8(u))
